recent_posts.title: How we replaced NGINX-Ingress at Stack Overflow
recent_posts.summary: Stack Overflow shares how they evaluated and replaced Ingress-NGINX after its retirement announcement. They narrowed candidates to three Kubernetes Gateway API implementations: NGINX Gateway Fabric, Traefik, and Istio. Testing covered functional use cases, RPS benchmarks at 10,000 requests/second, and route scaling up to 5,000 HTTPRoutes. Key findings: Traefik was significantly slower at converging large numbers of routes, NGINX showed latency spikes during route updates under load, while Istio performed consistently across all tests. Despite Istio's more complex syntax for advanced features like external authorization, Stack Overflow chose Istio for its stability, performance, and advanced feature set.

recent_posts.title: Dispatches from O'Reilly: Fast Paths and Slow Paths
recent_posts.summary: Autonomous AI systems at scale cannot rely on synchronous governance for every decision without collapsing under latency and coordination overhead. The solution is distinguishing fast paths (preauthorized, bound execution that proceeds without per-step approval) from slow paths (reserved for irreversible or high-stakes decisions). Control planes should observe continuously but intervene selectively, using feedback mechanisms like tightening thresholds or narrowing tool access rather than blocking execution. This approach treats governance as a feedback system rather than an approval workflow, allowing autonomy to scale while preserving safety and trust.

recent_posts.title: JavaScript Temporal proposal replaces the broken Date object
recent_posts.summary: The JavaScript Date object has long been a source of frustration for developers. Libraries like Moment.js offered relief but grew overly complex. The TC39 Temporal proposal, which took nine years to finalize, introduces a modern date/time API as a top-level namespace to replace Date in ECMAScript.

recent_posts.title: How a non-coder built an AI agent to top the Stack Overflow internal leaderboard
recent_posts.summary: A self-described non-coder at Stack Overflow builds an AI agent using Claude Code and the Stack Internal MCP server to automatically generate and post relevant Q&As, ultimately reaching #1 on the company's internal knowledge-sharing leaderboard. Along the way, the author explains MCP (Model Context Protocol) as a standardized bridge connecting LLMs to external data sources, replacing the need for custom API connectors. The piece blends a personal narrative with a beginner-friendly introduction to agentic AI concepts, vibe-coding, and the Stack Internal product.

recent_posts.title: Your LLM issues are really data issues
recent_posts.summary: Schema changes, inconsistent data definitions, and weak governance are root causes of LLM and analytics failures. Getting data AI-ready requires attention to metadata management, semantic consistency, and observability across the data ecosystem.

recent_posts.title: Turning scattered knowledge into trusted intelligence: Stack Internal 2026.3
recent_posts.summary: Stack Internal 2026.3 introduces the general availability of its Ingestion engine, which uses an AI pipeline to convert unstructured documents (PDFs, Markdown, Office files, images) and Confluence Cloud pages into structured, SME-verified Q&A pairs. The engine auto-tags, confidence-scores, and routes content to experts for final review, reducing manual curation burden. Validated knowledge is then accessible via an MCP server in AI tools and IDEs. All customers receive 100 Knowledge Objects per month at no extra cost.

recent_posts.title: AI enters the accountability phase as enterprise deployments demand real results
recent_posts.summary: A conference report from HumanX 2026 arguing that AI has moved past the experimental phase into a 'find out' stage where real business value must be demonstrated. Key themes include the shift from wonder to reliability and trust in enterprise AI deployments, the ballooning cost of token spend as agentic systems multiply, the challenge of monetization (even Anthropic and OpenAI don't expect profitability until 2028–2030), and growing social concerns about AI's psychological and economic effects. The piece highlights that hallucinations, identity/access controls, and observability are the main trust challenges, while multi-agent orchestration is driving costs up rapidly.

recent_posts.title: Black box AI drift and why AI coding tools make decisions nobody asked for
recent_posts.summary: A developer-turned-UX designer shares a year-long experience stress-testing AI coding assistants on a complex developer tool project. The core finding is 'black box AI drift' — the gap between what a developer intends and what AI silently implements. The AI built elaborate, unrequested systems, deleted work without warning, and produced confident-sounding but flawed output. The author argues that better prompts and downstream fixes aren't sufficient solutions; instead, AI tools need to become 'glass boxes' that surface their decisions and keep humans genuinely in control rather than just nominally in the loop.

recent_posts.title: How to get multiple agents to play nice at scale
recent_posts.summary: Engineers from Intuit discuss the challenges of coordinating multiple AI agents in complex systems at scale. Topics include automated evaluations to make agent behavior more predictable, trade-offs between agent swarms versus a single highly capable agent, and how real customer behavior influenced their technical architecture decisions.

recent_posts.title: Stack Overflow survey on AI agent use among software engineers
recent_posts.summary: Stack Overflow is conducting a survey on how software engineers are using AI agents in their work. The survey explores questions around agent autonomy, pricing models (per-token vs flat rate), and whether agents are genuinely helping developers. Results will be shared in May. The survey closes April 30.
